items.title: Take a short walk after meals
items.text: Your sugar rose about 18.1 mg/dL less after meals when you walked. Aim for 10 to 20 minutes after dinner, where the program saw the biggest gain (18.3 mg/dL). A check in real adults (CGMacros) pointed the same way, at about a fifth of the program's size, but it is not proven there yet.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: When you had dinner at 8 pm or later, your sugar rose about 9.2 mg/dL more than after earlier dinners. Try to start dinner before 8 pm to see how it affects your sugar.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 8.8 hours, which is something to consider when thinking about your sugar. You might look into how overnight fasting affects your sugar, but more research is needed to understand its impact.
